items.summary: A flaw was found in Kroxylicious. The ACL authorizer's rules-file parser unquotes `matching /…/` regular-expression literals using the string unquoting rules, which strips every backslash escape. As a result, an allow rule such as `matching /orders\.v1/` is compiled as the regex `orders.v1`, which also matches unintended names such as `ordersXv1`, and character classes such as `\d` and `\w` lose their special meaning. Allow rules written with regex escapes can therefore apply to more resources than the author intended. Depending on the ACL configuration, this may allow an authenticated Kafka client to access a resource (such as read or write a topic) that should have been denied.

The Streamit WordPress plugin before 1.3.10 does not perform any authorization or nonce verification on one of its unauthenticated AJAX routes, which invokes an attacker-supplied PHP function with an attacker-supplied argument array, allowing unauthenticated attackers to call arbitrary functions (for example to create an administrator account), leading to privilege escalation and remote code execution.

The WP Ultimate CSV Importer  WordPress plugin before 9.2 does not restrict the destination filename and extension, nor validate the fetched content type, when importing remote media, allowing an Administrator of a Multisite subsite to write and execute arbitrary PHP in the shared WordPress context despite not being a Network Administrator and being unable to install WP Ultimate CSV Importer  WordPress plugin before 9.2 or edit files.

The Widgets for Google Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, WP Tripadvisor Review Widgets WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Booking.com Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Reviews & Recommendations WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Airbnb Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Yelp Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Amazon Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Thumbtack Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Ebay Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Zillow Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Capterra Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Expedia Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Opentable Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for WordPress Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Hotels.com Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Review Widgets for Szallas.hu WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for AliExpress Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Árukereső Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Foursquare Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Alibaba Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for SourceForge Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3 do not sanitise and escape the connected business details before outputting them in their review widgets, which could allow users with the Editor role and above to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks even when the unfiltered_html capability is disallowed (for example in a multisite setup).

The Ahime Image Printer WordPress plugin through 1.0.0 does not validate the name, extension or type of uploaded files before writing them to disk, allowing unauthenticated attackers to upload arbitrary files, including PHP, and execute code on the server.

The Easy DragDrop File Uploader WordPress plugin before 1.1.10 does not validate a user-supplied path before deleting it, allowing unauthenticated users to delete arbitrary files and directories on the server, such as wp-config.php.
